title: Energetic channels in finite many-body quantum charging
authors: Dara Murphy, George Mihailescu, Anne Matthies, Irene D'Amico, Steve Campbell
abstract: We examine how a finite many-body system can function as an effective charger for a single-qubit quantum battery, using the Lipkin-Meshkov-Glick model as a paradigmatic setting. As our figure of merit, we consider the battery ergotropy while explicitly resolving the energetic flows across the composite system. In the absence of intra-charger interactions, we show that the generation of non-zero ergotropy is controlled by the competition between collective coupling and spectral mismatch. We further demonstrate that even passive positive-temperature charger states can generate finite battery ergotropy, provided the charger is sufficiently large and sufficiently hot. Intra-charger interactions restructure the charger spectrum and qualitatively modify the available energetic pathways. While they can enhance the amount of energy accessible for charging, they can simultaneously divert energy into internal many-body and battery-charger interaction channels, producing an energetic impedance to direct charger-to-battery transfer. Consequently, battery ergotropy alone is insufficient to characterize an effective many-body charger: the useful work generated and its energetic provenance must be assessed together.
summary: This paper analyzes how a complex, finite many-body system can act as a quantum charger for a simple qubit battery. Using the LMG model, the authors show that while energy transfer is possible, the presence of internal interactions creates an 'energetic impedance.' Therefore, simply measuring the extractable work (ergotropy) is insufficient; the full energy accounting is required to understand the charging mechanism.
main_problem: The paper investigates the fundamental conditions governing whether a finite many-body quantum system can effectively charge a single-qubit quantum battery.
main_result: The authors conclude that battery ergotropy alone is insufficient to characterize an effective charger; one must assess the useful work generated alongside its precise energetic provenance.
method: The analysis uses theoretical tools, including examining energy flows via commutators and analyzing the system's ergotropy, within the weak coupling limit.
model_or_system: The system consists of a single-qubit battery and a charger modeled by the Lipkin-Meshkov-Glick (LMG) model, coupled by an interaction Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Battery ergotropy (maximum extractable work), energy flow across the composite system, and the average energies of the battery, charger, and interaction terms.
important_parameters: Collective coupling strength ($g$), spectral mismatch ($\Delta = \omega_B - \omega_C$), and the size/temperature of the charger ($N$).
main_assumptions: The analysis often considers the weak battery-charger interaction limit ($g \ll \omega_B, \omega_C$) and analyzes the system dynamics by switching on/off the interaction term.

paper_structure:
The paper progresses by first analyzing the non-interacting case ($J=0$) to establish the role of spectral mismatch. It then introduces intra-charger interactions ($J 
eq 0$), showing how they restructure the spectrum and introduce energy impedance, leading to the final conclusion about necessary diagnostics.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the non-equilibrium energy dynamics in coupled quantum systems, which is central to understanding energy harvesting and quantum thermodynamics in AMO physics.
